subject: if-st-dy
title: IF.ST.DY.-----SOC.RT.
description: Diagram in SD(SY)-27 (Spectacle-Diversion Syndrome, Level One) accompanying Braxton's argument about the style of cultural movements: 'the most basic factor that determines the particulars of spectacle-diversion initiations has to do with the style of a given movement — rather than its intention.' (C)IF-ST-DY (infra-structure dynamics) is crossed with SOC-RT (social reality): the question is what infra-structure-dynamics produces when crossed with social-reality, given that style functions as the basic factor of spectacle-diversion. Off the main line, (R)TM (the reality of terminology—or terms of a definition) leads to INFO-DY (information dynamics), then to VT-PLT (vibrational platform) and on to ACT (activism). POL-DY (political dynamics) also branches from the main line and carries two chains: AFN (affinity negation) to APP-RDEF (applied redefinitions) to (R)INT (the reality of intention), and PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) to ACC-DY (accelerated dynamics) to (P)AGT (point of idea completion for agreement).
